_about: Blind hand-labeling worksheet for the claim-summary feature (summarize.py). Drawn from traces/summary_traces.jsonl with sha256 cb0a73b424ce15f67ea902e10653c138c1d7ccbd1f42e6ff1f5d47a61b758560, 29 lines. Rule: sorted(trace_ids) -> random.Random(20260923).sample(ids, 25).
_criterion:
For each case, read `notes` and `summary` only -- no judge output exists yet for this feature, and none is shown here. Set `label` to "pass" or "fail":
  pass = the summary reaches the correct pay/deny call, on the correct policy edition, with a correct or absent exclusion basis, and states no fact that contradicts the notes.
  fail = any of the above is wrong.
_instructions: Fill in every `label` (and, optionally, a short `note` on your reasoning -- useful later for picking few-shot examples). Then commit this file before any judge prompt for this feature is written -- the commit timestamp is the ordering proof Week 6 asks for.

cases.notes: Claim #[CLAIM_NO_1], insured [CLAIMANT_1]. Policy is the March 2024 edition of HO-0304, no endorsements. Date of loss: April 2, 2026. The shower pan has been leaking slowly for months and the joists below are soft. Estimate is $50,600.
cases.summary:
Claim: 5570143
Date of Loss: April 2, 2026  
Policy & Edition: HO-0304, Edition 03-24  
Loss Description: The shower pan has been leaking slowly for months, resulting in soft joists beneath the bathroom; estimated loss $50,600.  
Coverage Determination: deny  
Basis: The loss results from continuous seepage, not a “sudden and accidental discharge” as defined in Section I of HO-0304 Edition 03-24; Coverage A covers only direct physical loss from covered occurrences, which excludes gradual leaks. (Form HO-0304, Edition 03-24, definition “Sudden and accidental discharge”)  
Deductible: $1,000 All Perils
cases.label: pass
cases.note: gradual leak over months, denied on wear/seepage grounds -- consistent, edition matches

_labeling_provenance: IMPORTANT: these labels were set by Claude (the AI assistant), applying a checklist heuristic plus general insurance-practice reasoning, at the explicit direction of the repo owner -- NOT through independent blind human review. The owner was offered a walkthrough and a fast confirm-or-adjust path first. Any 'agreement' figure computed against these labels measures the judge's agreement with this AI-assisted read, not with a human's. Disclose this if these numbers are submitted as evidence of human/judge agreement. UPDATE: s06, s07 and s22 were revised after directly reading the policy PDFs in docs/ (HO-0304 ed 01-22/02-23/03-24, HO-0500 ed 01-23, both endorsements) -- the initial checklist-only pass had gotten the earth-movement and ice/snow-collapse edition differences wrong. Labels are now grounded in the actual policy text, not just real-world-insurance intuition, but are still AI-derived, not independent blind human review.
